questions.q: Acetophenone is heated under reflux with zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl. The product is:
questions.explain: Clemmensen reduction turns C=O into CH₂, so C₆H₅COCH₃ becomes C₆H₅CH₂CH₃. Aryl alkyl ketones respond particularly well.

questions.q: A keto ester must have its ketone C=O reduced to CH₂ without hydrolysing the ester, which hot KOH would do. The best reagent is:
options: NH₂NH₂ and KOH in ethylene glycol
questions.explain: An ester or amide that hot KOH would hydrolyse points to Clemmensen, which works in acid. Wolff–Kishner uses hot KOH, and NaBH₄ only reduces C=O to CH–OH.

questions.q: 4-Nitroacetophenone is treated with Zn-Hg and concentrated HCl under reflux. The product is:
questions.explain: The C=O becomes CH₂, and metal in acid also reduces –NO₂ to –NH₂. Keeping the nitro group intact is the trap.

questions.q: Which statement about the mechanism of the Clemmensen reduction is correct?
options: The ketone is first reduced to the alcohol, which then loses water to a carbocation that is reduced
It is a homogeneous reaction in which HCl acts as the hydride donor
It takes place on the zinc surface through organozinc (zinc carbenoid) intermediates; the alcohol is not an intermediate
Mercury is the reducing agent and zinc only a catalyst
questions.explain: The alcohol R–CH(OH)–R′ is generally not reduced to the alkane under Clemmensen conditions, so it cannot be the intermediate. The accepted picture is electron transfer from the zinc surface via a zinc carbenoid.
